item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract: its Upload implementation uses the established multipart helper and delegates directly to FilesService.Add, preserving centralized option, request, response, and error behavior. B has stronger Upload tests, but explicitly violates the required architecture and scope by duplicating Add and changing generic raw/retry behavior.","reasons":["A calls multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content) and passes the resulting replayable body through s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), exactly matching the required repository pattern.","A preserves FilesService.Add unchanged and demonstrates retrying an upload sourced from a non-seekable reader.","B reimplements FilesService.Add inside Upload, including option processing, headers, Raw.Do, response decoding, and missing-data handling. This directly violates the requirement to route through Add and creates duplicate machinery that can drift.","B makes broad changes to RawClient.Do, body ownership, seek handling, content length, and retry semantics despite the contract explicitly excluding unrelated request/retry refactoring. Its documentation also expands the promised behavior beyond the requested Upload API."],"risks_a":["A adds the unrelated PersonsService.UploadPicture API and tests, violating scope discipline and the instruction to add exactly the specified convenience API.","A's multipart test checks the field and filename but never verifies uploaded content.","A lacks the required tests for empty filename, nil content, and source-reader failures, although the implementation visibly validates and propagates those errors."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, duplicating its logic and risking future behavioral divergence.","The generic ReadSeeker retry change is out of scope and introduces subtle shared-seeker and body-lifecycle semantics across RawClient callers.","B still lacks a source-reader failure test required by the contract, despite otherwise broader validation and multipart coverage."]}
